title: How Many Days in Krka National Park? 2027 Guide
metaDescription: One day is enough for Krka National Park. See what 1 day, 2–3 days and longer give you, day-trip options, and how to fit Krka into a 7- or 10-day Croatia trip.
content:
## How Many Days Do You Need in Krka National Park?

One day is the right amount for almost every traveler. Krka National Park is built around one main site, Skradinski buk, a set of 17 travertine cascades with wooden boardwalks. The loop takes 2–4 hours. Two other sights, Visovac island and Roški slap, extend the visit to a full day. Krka is much smaller in scope than Plitvice, so a multi-day park stay is rarely needed.

The park is in North Dalmatia, near Šibenik. It is about 85 km (roughly one hour by road) from Split.

## What You Can See in 1 Day

One day is enough for Skradinski buk and one boat excursion. Choose based on how much time you have:

- **Half day (2–4 hours):** Skradinski buk boardwalks only. Entry costs €7 from November to March, €20 in April, May and October, and €40 from June to September. Adults pay €30 after 15:00 in peak months.
- **Most of a day (5–6 hours):** Skradinski buk plus the Visovac island boat. The boat costs €15 for adults and stops 30 minutes at the island monastery.
- **Full day (8–9 hours):** Skradinski buk, Visovac and Roški slap on the 4-hour boat excursion. It costs €20–25 on top of entry, depending on the route.

The entry ticket includes the Skradin–Skradinski buk boat and the Lozovac shuttle bus, but only from 1 April to 31 October. The Visovac and Roški slap boats are sold on site and cannot be booked online, so keep some cash or a card ready.

Swimming is banned at Skradinski buk. It is allowed only at Roški slap, Stinice and Pisak (Remetić), and only from 1 June to 30 September. Anyone expecting a waterfall swim at the main site should look elsewhere.

## What 2–3 Days Add

A second day only makes sense if you want the quieter upstream park. Roški slap, with its string of small cascades, is reachable by road from Šibenik, Drniš, Knin and Skradin. The Roški slap/Burnum/Kistanje sector has its own cheaper ticket (€20 adult in summer, €12 in April, May and October, €7 in winter). The Burnum Roman military camp and the Krka Monastery boat (€20, 2 hours, departing from Roški slap) sit in the same area.

A second night is also useful for logistics. Staying in Skradin or Šibenik lets you arrive at 08:00 opening, before tour buses, and avoid the long July and August boat queues from Skradin.

Three days is too long for the park itself. Use the extra time for Šibenik (the St. James Cathedral is a UNESCO site) or the coast nearby.

## Longer Stay: When It Makes Sense

Four days or more suits hikers, photographers and travelers using the Šibenik area as a base. The park has about 47 km of marked trails. Winter visits are possible but limited: Skradinski buk runs 9:00–16:00 and there are no boats, so you arrive by car at Lozovac. The park closes 25–26 December.

## Can Krka Be a Day Trip?

Yes. Krka is among the easiest national park day trips in Croatia.

- **From Split:** about 85 km, roughly one hour by car. Organised tours cost around €50–70 with transport and entry. Dubrovnik tours cost more and take far longer, so they are a poor use of a day.
- **From Šibenik or Skradin:** 15 minutes or less. This is the best option for avoiding crowds.
- **From Zadar:** about 1 to 1.5 hours by car.

This is one of those things that sounds great until you try it: a Split tour that packs Krka, a winery stop and a town visit into one day. You get a hurried hour at the falls in the hottest, busiest part of the day. A rental car or a self-planned trip, at opening or after 15:00, is a better use of €40.

## Fitting Krka into a 7-Day Croatia Route

Give Krka one day, ideally as a stop between Zadar and Split, or between Split and the north. A typical 7-day coastal route is Dubrovnik–Split–Krka stop–Zadar, or the reverse. Use Šibenik or Skradin as a single overnight, or drive Krka as a mid-journey stop with luggage in the car. Leaving the park by about 15:00 in summer keeps the transfer manageable.

## Fitting Krka into a 10-Day Croatia Route

Ten days allows one night near the park, which removes the early-start pressure. Spend that night in Šibenik, then do Krka at opening time. Use the extra days for Plitvice Lakes or an island such as Hvar or Korčula. Krka and Plitvice are separate parks, and Croatia has no combined pass.

## Best Time of Year

Spring (April–May) and October give the best balance of water flow, boat service and a €20 ticket. July and August are hot and crowded, with the highest price. In summer, the 08:00 opening or the post-15:00 ticket is the practical choice.

## Recommendation by Traveler Type

- **First-timers:** One full day, Skradinski buk plus the Visovac boat. Base in Šibenik or Split.
- **Families:** One day, with the Skradinski buk loop and no Roški slap boat. Children up to 7 enter free and ages 7–18 pay reduced rates (€15 in summer). Plan a late start and a rest stop. Swimming is only allowed at Roški slap in summer.
- **Couples:** Two days if you want a quiet visit. Stay one night in Skradin, do the falls at opening, then visit Roški slap by car.
- **Beach holiday:** Half a day, after 15:00 in summer for the €30 ticket. Swimming at Skradinski buk is not allowed, so treat Krka as a break from the coast.

faq.question: Is one day enough for Krka National Park?
faq.answer: Yes. One day covers Skradinski buk and a Visovac boat trip, which takes 5–6 hours. Add Roški slap on the 4-hour boat excursion and the full visit runs 8–9 hours.

faq.question: How much does Krka National Park cost in 2027?
faq.answer: The 2026 adult ticket is €7 from November to March, €20 in April, May and October, and €40 from June to September. After 15:00 in peak months it is €30. Check the park's official site for 2027 prices before you go.

faq.question: Can you do Krka as a day trip from Split?
faq.answer: Yes. The park is about 85 km from Split, roughly one hour by road. Organised tours cost around €50–70, and a rental car lets you arrive at 08:00 opening or after 15:00.

faq.question: Should I spend the night near Krka?
faq.answer: It is worth it in July and August. Staying in Šibenik or Skradin lets you arrive before the crowds and skip long boat queues. Outside summer, a day trip from Split or Zadar works fine.

faq.question: Can you swim in Krka National Park?
faq.answer: Swimming at Skradinski buk has been banned since 2021. It is allowed only at Roški slap, Stinice and Pisak (Remetić), from 1 June to 30 September.

faq.question: Is Krka or Plitvice better if I only have time for one?
faq.answer: Krka is easier to fit into a coastal trip, being about an hour from Split. Plitvice is larger and needs more time, and it is further inland. Choose Krka for a day trip and Plitvice if you have time for a longer inland detour.

quickAnswer: Plan one full day in Krka National Park. That covers Skradinski buk, the boardwalks and a Visovac boat trip. Add a second night only to see Roški slap and Burnum, or to stay in Šibenik or Skradin. Krka works well as a day trip from Split, Zadar or Šibenik, so most travelers need no more than one overnight.
